payload.content:
# Pantry design

## Local ownership

The app is a single local browser page with no account, application server or remote service.
TypeScript is compiled into one classic browser bundle, allowing index.html to open directly.
The bundle has no runtime dependencies.
A framework would add runtime and build conventions without improving this first journey.
The app stores one household’s named supplies and needed marks in local storage.
Browser storage is tied to the page location and browser profile; moving the page does not migrate data.
The initial supported browser is installed Google Chrome on Linux, exercised directly by the checks.

## Responsibilities and flow

src/pantry.ts is the public interface and owns item identity, needed-state transitions and a single session state.
src/private/storage.ts owns storage acquisition, format validation, loading and saving behind that interface.
src/ui/render.ts renders the public snapshot and forwards explicit add, needed and retry-save actions.
src/main.ts assembles the public pantry and UI.
The flow is browser action -> public pantry mutation -> private save attempt -> public snapshot -> DOM rendering.
Only the pantry controls the canonical session state; snapshots cannot mutate it.

## UI boundary

UI code imports only ../pantry.js, the public interface, and never private storage.
UI code never accesses localStorage directly, including bare, property and destructuring forms.
Browser rendering APIs such as document.createElement and window.requestAnimationFrame are permitted.
The native ESLint configuration is the executable source of these restrictions.
Static imports and exports are restricted; dynamic imports and require are rejected in UI code.
Computed runtime indirection, eval and malicious aliasing require review; these checks are not a sandbox.
There are no boundary exceptions in version one.
The rule protects visible saving status from bypasses and keeps persistence failures in one owner.

## Reliability and errors

Adding an empty trimmed name fails visibly without changing the item list.
Equivalent full names reuse the item and preserve its existing needed mark.
Distinct full supplied names remain separate items.
Needed means intention to buy, never a stock measurement.
Storage reads validate the saved array, names, duplicate identities and boolean marks.
If acquisition, parsing, loading or saving fails, the current session remains usable and displays an unsaved warning.
Only a successful save permits claiming that changes will survive reload.
Retry saving is an explicit local action; there is no remote fallback.
No runtime configuration or external service is required.

## Acceptance

Add Rice, mark it needed, view Rice on the shopping list, reload and retain it.
Re-add “ rice ” without creating a duplicate or clearing its needed mark.
Brown Rice and White Rice remain distinct full supplied names.
When saving throws, continued edits work and unsaved changes are visible; successful retry restores honest saved status and reload retention.
Valid browser rendering and public-interface imports pass the same native lint command that rejects private imports and direct storage access.

## Review standards and change locality

Accept changes against VISION.md and use GLOSSARY.md for domain meanings.
A shopping presentation change belongs to src/ui/render.ts and its browser cases.
A storage format change belongs to src/private/storage.ts and persistence cases; it must preserve the public interface or receive explicit review.
These two expected changes need no shared registry; their common contract is the public snapshot.
No measured co-change benefit is claimed because there is no project history.
Exceptions need an owner-approved reason, narrow scope and removal condition before implementation.
No existing debt baseline is needed because this is a new foundation.
Formatting, lint, strict type checks, public behaviour checks and actual browser checks are required through npm run check.
Checks establish the selected cases, while reviewers judge scope, meaning and new browser indirection.

## Maintenance

.bstack/project.json registers authoritative documents, rules, scopes, acceptance sources and the native check.
.bstack/bin/bstack-check.mjs is the installed dependency-free standalone checker, requiring Node 24 and Git but no installed skill.
For local review, use an explicit comparison base and the single reviewed .bstack/assessment.json record.
Commit implementation, collect portable evidence, assess every candidate and unmapped path with literal authoritative citations, bind the reviewed fingerprint, and commit the assessment separately.
Run the standalone checker in this checkout and a different-root clean clone with isolated home and cache.
Its required leaf is npm run check; development dependencies and installed Chrome remain native-check prerequisites.
No hosted CI, release or delivery service is selected.

# Pantry language

## Item

An item is one named pantry supply.
Names are trimmed; case-insensitive full-name matches identify the same item.
Brown Rice and White Rice are distinct supplied names.

## Needed

Needed records the household’s intention to buy an item, independently of stock.
Re-adding an equivalent name preserves that mark; only an explicit needed-state change alters it.
There are no quantities or stock levels.

## Shopping list

The shopping list contains the items currently marked needed.

## Unsaved changes

Unsaved changes are current session changes that have not been successfully saved.
They remain usable in the session but are not promised to survive reload.

# Pantry list

A local household pantry and shopping list. No account or application server.

## Setup and use

Require Linux, Node 24 or later, npm, Git and Google Chrome on PATH as google-chrome.
Run `npm ci`, then `npm run build`, and open index.html in Chrome.
Add Rice, mark it needed, open Shopping list, and reload to retain it after successful saving.
Keep the page location and browser profile stable for local storage.
When saving fails, the page keeps session work and labels it unsaved; use Retry saving when storage works again.

## Checks

`npm run check` runs resource verification, formatting, native lint, strict TypeScript checks, bundle build, public behaviour tests and real browser tests.
`npm run journey` runs resource verification, build and real browser tests.
`npm run lint` runs only resource verification and native boundary/general lint.
`npm run format` formats maintained source and guidance; the installed checker and package lock retain original bytes.
Before each Node suite, the Linux resource guard requires at least 8 GB available memory and disk, load below 36 and at most two host-wide suites including this run.
Tests run against a fresh disposable Chrome profile and the actual local page, without a web server.
Each browser run captures JSON observations and screenshots in a unique scratch directory and prints its path.
The checks do not establish compatibility with other browsers or every reflective runtime storage bypass.

## Authority and maintenance

[VISION.md](VISION.md) owns purpose and non-goals, [GLOSSARY.md](GLOSSARY.md) domain meaning, and [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) responsibilities and review expectations.
The native tool configurations own executable settings.
.bstack/project.json maps change paths to these sources and npm run check.
The unchanged installed standalone checker runs with `node .bstack/bin/bstack-check.mjs --repo . --base <base> --assessment .bstack/assessment.json --json`.
Create a change-specific portable assessment against an explicit ancestor, review its semantic claims and exact fingerprint, commit it separately, and run the checker in this checkout and a fresh different-root clone with isolated home/cache.
There is no selected hosted CI or delivery service.

payload.content:
# Pantry list vision

## Purpose and responsibility
Pantry list helps a household remember its pantry supplies and what it needs to buy.
It owns a local record of named supplies and a shopping list derived from the supplies marked needed.
These commitments come from the owner’s confirmed intent for version one, rather than existing project history.

## Household scope
Version one runs locally in a browser using TypeScript and local storage.
It requires no account, server or remote service.
Accept changes that improve the household’s ability to record supplies and see what it needs to buy.
Resist changes that make this local journey depend on a remote system or expand it into household account management.

## Named supplies and shopping intent
An item is one named pantry supply.
The shopping list contains items marked as needing to buy.
The needed mark records the household’s intention to buy independently of whether the supply is present.
The household controls that mark as a shopping decision; it is not inferred from stock.
Names are trimmed, and a case-insensitive match on the full supplied name reuses the existing item.
Re-adding an equivalent full name preserves the existing needed mark; only an explicit needed-state change alters that shopping decision.
Brown Rice and White Rice remain distinct supplies because their full supplied names differ.
Quantities and stock levels are outside version one.

## Trustworthy local use
The first useful journey is to add Rice, mark it needed, view Rice on the shopping list, and reload with that decision retained.
The interface tells the household whether its changes have been saved.
When local storage saving fails, the current session remains usable and unsaved changes are visible.
Reload retention is claimed only after local saving succeeds.
Accept reliability changes that preserve useful local work and make persistence limits visible.

## Contribution tests
A change aligns when it makes named supplies and needed purchases easier to manage locally while preserving an honest account of saved state.
Resist a change when it requires quantities, stock accounting, accounts, a server or remote services to complete this journey, or obscures whether local work is retained.
